memory_candidates.content: When auditing whether a behavioral divergence between two code paths is intentional design or an unreviewed assertion, apply the independent-corroboration test: does the OTHER path's own handler implement the divergence in its own code, or does only a shared classifier/table assert it? A divergence implemented independently by both sides' handlers is a design (keep it, document the justification). A divergence asserted only in one shared table -- especially one citing an untraceable historical decision -- is an unreviewed assertion (converge it). This test cleanly separated two superficially identical rows in the same routing table, where one row was a real semantic difference and the other was a latent defect.

When adding a new pre-dispatch probe call that reuses a helper script originally built for post-dispatch staleness gating (e.g. orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh's window_start_ts), pass a distinct, explicitly-named zero/disabled value (e.g. prior_meta_probe_window=0) rather than reusing the existing post-dispatch variable name. Reusing the name silently binds the new call to semantics ('current dispatch's window') that do not apply to the new pre-dispatch call shape ('prior cycle's leftover state, regardless of age'). Name the variable for what IT represents, not what the shared helper's other callers call their argument.
